headline: Both rounds found leads that visibly pay for enquiries (live Meta ads, fresh RERA registrations) but never observed the need itself: 22 leads, 0 observed slow replies, 0 replies from the 9 contacted so far (as of 19 Oct 14:40 IST). Round 1 (Apify, 14 agents, ~34 min, ~2.2M tokens, ~US$2.85) and round 2 (free, 26 agents, 63 min, ~4.1M tokens) gave leads of similar quality, and what actually raised quality was the adversarial skeptic, the independent fact-check and cheap deterministic checks (MX, site fingerprint, send-day ad recheck), not more scouts. Next campaign: script those gates, qualify just-in-time instead of ahead of the pipeline, and send in a way that lets grade and hunger score be calibrated against real replies.

lessons.lesson: Grades and the hunger score measure 'pays for enquiries and is reachable', not 'needs us'; need was never observed for any of the 22 leads, and the current send plan cannot calibrate the score because everything sent is Hungry 7-8.
lessons.evidence: memory.md sections M and 2026-10-19 ~12:00 ('need is inferred, not observed' in both rounds); _research_raw_r2.json Swagat case_against ('A holds on they pay for enquiries, NOT on they answer slowly'). Wave 1 sent only the 5 Hungry leads (Pride 8, Rivanta 8, Brij 7, Elenza 7, NB 7) and left 4 Warm + 1 Cold unsent; wave 2 is again 7-8 (Great Spaces 8, Swagat 7, Parshwanath 7, Space Age 7). R2 tiers: 9 of 12 Hungry; Nitya Buildcon with ZERO paid ads still scored 6; SuperCITY scored 8 but is grade B. Result so far: 0 replies from 9 contacted leads (sends.jsonl, memory 16-19 Oct), so the playbook section 5 plan 'compare Hungry vs Warm reply rate' cannot happen.
lessons.do_next_time: Rename it a pay-signal score and compute it in code from separate sub-scores (pay observed / fit / reachability / resistance), each backed by url + date; write the predicted tier into the lead entry BEFORE the send; put 1-2 Warm leads into every wave as controls; after N days compute reply and page-open rate per tier and per source. Until a few replies exist, call every tier 'unvalidated'. Add the stronger public probes already listed in memory section O (Facebook 'typically replies within' badge, unanswered price comments under ads, review replies, telecaller hiring) when Apify credit exists.

lessons.lesson: First-pass qualifier grades are inflated and scraper-only grades flip on a live re-check; the adversarial skeptic using a different method is the real quality gate, so run it on every A and every score >= 7.
lessons.evidence: _research_raw_r2.json: 8 of 12 qualifiers graded A first; the skeptic kept 2 (Great Spaces, Swagat) and lowered 6 (SuperCITY, Rameshwar, Space Age, Nyalkaran, CS Group, Swarna) = 75%. _research_raw.json: only Brij was graded A and the skeptic lowered it, so round 1 ended 0 A / 10 B. agent/state/leads/trigger_leads_2026-10-14.csv (Apify round 5) graded 5 real-estate rows A (1 Clik, Rameshwar, Lions, Parshwanath, Swarna); on 19 Oct with the browser they came back B, B, not qualified, B, B (Swarna 6 Warm, with an in-house CRM found at -2). Scout claims also failed on re-read: NB 'no WhatsApp/phone/email on homepage' (truncated WebFetch text) and Beverlynn 'no official website' were both wrong; Swagat Group (Ahmedabad, has a Kenyt.ai bot) was wrongly bundled with Swagat Developers (Surat).
lessons.do_next_time: Make the challenge stage mandatory and independent: re-open the Ad Library live, fetch raw HTML with curl instead of a model-summarised WebFetch, and treat scout text as claims. Cap a grade at B unless there are two independent dated observations, a verified identity and a working contact route. Never carry a scraper-only grade (the 13 A of 14 Oct) into a wave without a live re-check. Keep the 'Hungry' number out of the skeptic's blind spot: re-score it after the challenge (SuperCITY stayed 8 after being lowered).

lessons.lesson: Source yield: live Meta Ad Library cards are the best pay signal and GujRERA filtered to business-email promoters is the best free list; Google Maps, web search and domain guessing returned almost nothing, and 'free' round 2 was partly seeded by the Apify pool.
lessons.evidence: _research_raw.json gmaps scout: 200 places, 81 reviews from 29 places, 4 keyword-filtered reviews, 0 complaints about replies within 90 days, ~US$1.0 of the US$2.85. _research_raw_r2.json: WebSearch 'does not index fresh projects'; ~40,000 + ~20,000 + ~150 domain probes mostly hit namesakes; web-ahd-gnr gave 1 qualified lead (Satyagrah, Warm, no live ads), web-rest 0. GujRERA: exact-phrase Ad Library search of 140 fresh project names found ads for 1 project, but joining on the RERA-number token worked (Beverlynn); only 7/159, ~4/99 and 4/139 fresh promoters have a business-domain email, yet that filter surfaced Great Spaces (R2's top lead, A/8, a wave-2 send). pool-recheck was R2's most productive scout (5 of 12 qualified, 4 by found_in plus Parshwanath inferred, including 2 of the 4 wave-2 sends). Apify: ~1,500 ad rows for ~US$1.0 with snapshot.cta_type == WHATSAPP_MESSAGE as a machine filter, versus the browser's ~30 cards per query (~150 advertisers seen, only ~20 with a website).
lessons.do_next_time: Pipeline: (1) bulk advertiser list from the Ad Library (Apify when credit exists: US$5-10 is cheaper than the model tokens; browser otherwise), (2) GujRERA approvedDate window + business-email-domain filter + RERA-number-token Ad Library join as a second list, (3) browser verification of the top N advertiser pages only. Drop Maps-for-complaints and web-search launch discovery. Re-check the previous round's near-misses first.

lessons.lesson: 'Free' round 2 cost about twice the time and tokens per round and starved a shared tool quota; use scripts for deterministic work, reserve agents for judgement, and run a budget preflight before launching.
lessons.evidence: Round 1: 14 agents, ~34 min, ~2.2M sub-agent tokens, ~US$2.85 Apify (scout estimates 0.35 + 1.5 + 1.0) for 10 qualified leads = ~220K tokens/lead. Round 2: 26 agents, 63 min, ~4.1M tokens, US$0 for 12 qualified = ~342K tokens/lead (memory.md section M; entry 2026-10-19 ~12:00). R2 gaps fields: Great Spaces (an A lead) 'WebSearch budget was exhausted before I started', Swagat 'WebSearch hit its shared call limit', Space Age and Satyagrah the same, so the two A leads were graded with no web search. Round 1 hit Apify's monthly hard limit mid-run (~US$0.17 left, a 114-query Maps run refused, the Maps Q&A scrape never run) while the campaign budget was US$15 with ~US$3 used (operator message 17 Oct). Weekly Claude limit was 94-95% used on 15-16 Oct (memory.md). Scouts spent agent time on ~60,000 domain probes and RERA scans that a script does in seconds.
lessons.do_next_time: Before launch check remaining Apify credit and search quota; implement GujRERA pulls, domain/MX/HTML fingerprinting and ad-card parsing as tested scripts that agents call; stagger qualifiers after scouts or reserve quota for them; write tokens, minutes and dollars per phase into a campaign cost file so 'cost per qualified lead' and 'cost per reply' are real numbers.

lessons.lesson: 'Business-published contact' is not 'working contact': verify mailboxes by DNS before use, treat published WhatsApp numbers as unverified enquiry lines, and expect shared role inboxes instead of decision makers.
lessons.evidence: Contacts files: round 1 leads 4 of 10 had only free-mail (Pride, Rivanta, Silver, Somnath), round 2 2 of 12 (1 Clik, Nitya); Pride's only email is the RERA promoter Gmail copied by an aggregator (case_against). sends.jsonl/email_status.json: 8 of 9 first-touch emails delivered, Elenza's published sales@ address bounced on 16 Oct. R2 MX check (nslookup, done by hand by the operator after the workflow): swarnagroup.in has NO MX, SuperCITY's MX points to itself. WhatsApp: 0 of 3 cold template sends delivered (Brij 131049 five seconds after send, NB 131026 number cannot receive, Elenza no status after 16 h) although all 22 qualifiers wrote best_channel = email first (10/10, 12/12) and 19 explicitly warned against a cold template. Every email used is a role inbox (info@, sales@, office@, inquiry@). GujRERA register emails are ~94% gmail (150/159) and the register also holds PAN/personal ID fields.
lessons.do_next_time: Add a deterministic contact gate before qualification output counts a lead as reachable: MX lookup, role/free/business classification, verified_at date, suppression check. Flag every published WhatsApp number 'enquiry line, unverified' and use it only for lead-initiated chats or human 1:1 messages; send free-mail-only leads to the human-call lane (as done for Pride). Never store whole register records (PAN etc.); keep contacts in local files only.

lessons.lesson: Ad evidence goes stale within days and a one-day burst is ambiguous: store observation dates, require two observations, and re-verify on send day; never use scraper totals as counts.
lessons.evidence: Swagat Cilantra's ads were 21 hours old when qualified (_research_raw_r2.json) and ~1 day old at the 19 Oct 14:08 email; Space Age's WhatsApp poster ad dated 18 Oct; Pride's ~180 ads all started 9-10 Oct (one burst) and the first email left 17 Oct. Of 11 names from the 14 Oct Apify pool, Matangi (4 WhatsApp ads started 9 Oct) and Nalsafari (13 Oct) could not be found 5 days later and Arrows One and Alisha were dropped = 4 of 11 failed. Apify under-counted versus the browser (Swarna 1 vs 13, 1 Clik 9 vs 20, Madhav Reality 1 vs 11, Space Age 1 vs 8) and its 'total' showed an identical 175 for Brij and Pride (capped). The 30-second send-day recheck (wave2-adlib-recheck) found all 4 wave-2 leads send_as_is; page QA pass 2 noted there was no fallback copy if an ad is paused.
lessons.do_next_time: Every ad fact carries first_seen and observed_at; 'Hungry' needs ads seen twice >= 48 h apart or older than ~3 days (younger = 'burst, unproven'); make the send-day Ad Library recheck an automatic gate with prepared fallback wording; expire pool entries after ~3 days without a recheck; ignore scraper 'total' and per-advertiser counts from bulk actors, take counts only from the advertiser page.

lessons.lesson: Every sentence that reaches a hook, page or console summary must trace to a dated, quoted observation; run the independent fact-check inside the research flow and re-sync console text after it.
lessons.evidence: _wave2_factcheck.json (4 agents, ~9 min, ~0.5M tokens, run before building) corrected: 'book a site visit' is Novarra wording, not Aaroham; '4B3HK' is the developer's own label, not 3/4 BHK; 'Aaroham' collides with Ashiana Aaroham (Gurugram); Parshwanath is 2 BHK only and the FB.ME destination is unknown (never say 'lead form'); Space Age is a reseller of Arvind Sensora plots (not BHK), no GujRERA record for Sensora, ~87 competing resellers; Swagat: only 2 of 3 ads have the WhatsApp button and they do not name Cilantra. _page_qa_r2_pass2.json still found the premise 'your WhatsApp ads' unsupported for Great Spaces and Parshwanath. Conflict: the R1 scout and R2 qualifier read Cordelia's RERA approval of 12 Oct, the fact-check 'could not verify' it. r2_overrides.json (pushed to the console before the fact-check) still says Parshwanath ads 'promise a site visit through a Facebook lead form' and Swagat 'Cordelia RERA-registered 12 Oct'; console_patch.json only added page_url and history. Wave 1: Pride 'every tap to one WhatsApp chat' and Rivanta 'many ads invite WhatsApp' (one ad had the button) were caught only by claims review/preflight.
lessons.do_next_time: Dossier schema: observed_facts[{text, url, date, quote}] separate from hypotheses; add a field whatsapp_path = observed | possible | unknown (CTA type actually seen) and generate hooks per tag; put the fact-check between qualify and console push for any lead entering a wave; generate console entries from the fact-checked dossier (single source) instead of hand-written overrides; settle the Cordelia conflict with one direct GujRERA API call.

lessons.lesson: The pipeline lost provenance and reusable knowledge: key a persistent seen-ledger on canonical IDs, carry candidate IDs through qualification, and count independent sources only.
lessons.evidence: found_in is empty for 10 of 10 leads in _research_raw.json and for 3 of 12 in _research_raw_r2.json (Great Spaces, Swagat, Parshwanath = both A leads) because the join used norm(qualifier's rewritten business name); source attribution had to be inferred from scout notes. campaign-lead-research-r2.js scores sourceCount*3, so pool-recheck + meta-adlib-browser counted as two sources for Rameshwar and Swarna although both read the same Ad Library. 22 of 34 R2 candidates (65%) were never qualified (cheap score only). Near-miss lists (R1: Atmiya, Krishna Developers, Shivay, Shagun, Subhanu, Caladium, Suvidha, Shreenathji, Panth Park; R2: Vihav, Satyamev, Narayan, Revanta and ~16 phone-only click-to-WhatsApp advertisers) are free text in did_not_work, so nothing was reusable; R1's advice to run the Ad Library once per new RERA-number token was not tried in R2. What worked: normalised-name exclusion with substring match only for names of 6+ letters, alias strings (Om Infra 'Rivanta Victorious', Raghav Developers) skipped on sight, entity confusions (Rivanta firms, Swagat Group vs Developers, 'Pride') caught by qualifiers.
lessons.do_next_time: Keep agent/state/campaigns/seen.jsonl keyed by RERA promoterId / Facebook page ID / domain / phone last-10 with status, reason, date and source; scouts return a stable id, qualifiers echo it; cluster sources by underlying system (Ad Library, RERA, web) before scoring; when a round comes up short, revisit logged near-misses before launching new scouts.

lessons.lesson: Pace discovery to what can be built, sent and measured: research outran the pipeline, with 13 of 22 leads unsent and no wave-1 replies when round 2 was launched.
lessons.evidence: The operator's own 17 Oct advice (no new leads until the existing 10 are used and wave results are known; 6 leads still unused) was overridden by the owner's request on 19 Oct and the 10:52 IST start message lists filters but not that rule. R2 result at ~11:56 IST; 4 emails sent 14:07-14:09 IST after two QA passes (~7 min and ~0.5M tokens each, ~25 issues fixed). By 14:40 IST: 22 leads in the console, 9 contacted (Elenza, Brij, NB, Pride, Rivanta + Great Spaces, Swagat, Parshwanath, Space Age), 13 not (Beverlynn, Lotus, Somnath, Trinetra, Silver + 8 from R2), 0 replies. The bottleneck is per-lead assets (5 min render each, page, QA), Gujarati voice for the 5 Gujarati/mixed leads and 8 OK codes, not discovery. The R2 top-up trigger (fewer than 8 A/B leads with email) never fired (11 usable).
lessons.do_next_time: Stop rule: do not start a round while the unsent A/B pool is >= 2x the next wave's capacity or while the last wave is younger than the agreed decision window without a recorded decision. Keep a cheap candidate backlog and qualify just-in-time (when a lead is next in line, with the send-day recheck) instead of qualifying 12 ahead; log the stop reason in memory.md.

lessons.lesson: Resistance (an existing CRM, bot or agency) can be detected by a script on the candidate's own HTML and JS in seconds; run it before paying for a qualifier.
lessons.evidence: _research_raw_r2.json scout notes: Courtyard Group rejected (site form posts to crm.courtyardgroup.in), Vasantara Skies (Make.com webhook, date/time picker, promises a WhatsApp reply), Kaavyaratna / Shreenilay / Saamarth ('Powered by SAI' chatbot), Shree Buildcon ('AI' assistant), Swagat Group (Kenyt.ai), Vihav (about 17 lines and ~25 mailboxes). Swarna (own /api/submit-lead plus Firebase project 'swarna-group-crm') was only found at qualification and scored -2 after a full qualifier run. Round 1: Beverlynn (leads.beverlynn.in CRM), Lotus ('source:24' payload). Pixel/GTM/AW tags, utm hidden fields and WordPress REST page dates also worked as spend and freshness proxies when the Ad Library was unavailable (Great Spaces).
lessons.do_next_time: Write a fingerprint script run on every candidate website before qualification: fbq/GTM/AW tags, utm hidden fields, 'crm.' / 'api_lead' / webhook hosts, chat-widget vendor strings, Firebase/Supabase project names, sitemap lastmod. Auto-penalise a confirmed CRM or bot and store the evidence URL in the dossier.

lessons.lesson: In this segment 'reachable by email' and 'needs automation' pull in opposite directions: requiring a business email selects the more digital developers, who often already automate, while phone-only click-to-WhatsApp advertisers are unreachable by email.
lessons.evidence: _research_raw_r2.json meta-adlib-browser scout: of ~150 Gujarat real-estate advertisers only ~20 own a website (the only ones with an email); 16 phone-only click-to-WhatsApp advertisers were named and held back (Pradhan Glenforest, Pradhan Altiss, Sunfin, Radheshyam Luxuria, Vatsalya Hilltop, Titaanium Bungalows, Shiv Shakti Homes, Madhav Vila, Aadeshwar Avenue, Dream Land, Matru Group, Dev Aashish Group, Amogha, Zanzar, Karm Group, Shreem Group). The R2 merge score adds +2 for a published email. At least 9 developers with websites were rejected for existing automation (see CRM/bot list above). Email-first reached 8 of 9 inboxes but 0 replies; Pride, a phone-first lead with a free-mail address, produced the only page open + video play (19 Oct 09:10 IST, possibly a team visit).
lessons.do_next_time: Treat phone-first leads as a separate lane (owner's team calls, as done for Pride) and run a small pilot of 3 such advertisers next to the email lane; compare reply rates by lane before deciding the filter. Do not let the email bonus silently decide who gets researched.

mistakes_we_made: Round 1 had no hunger rubric in the qualifier schema: the 0-10 score and the Hungry/Warm/Cold waves were assigned by hand afterwards from stored evidence (memory.md section O), so rounds 1 and 2 are not scored the same way and wave 1 had no control group.
Round 1 launched three Apify scouts with US$3 caps each without checking remaining credit; the monthly hard limit hit mid-run (~US$0.17 left, Maps run refused, Maps Q&A scrape never done).

No deliverability check on round-1 emails: Elenza's published sales@ address bounced on the first send. The MX check in round 2 was done by the operator by hand after the workflow, not inside it; I found no record that the 17 Oct plan to verify the older pool's addresses was carried out.

Hooks and page claims went beyond the evidence in wave 1 (Pride 'every tap to one WhatsApp chat', Rivanta 'many ads invite WhatsApp', 'your ads' as a premise) and were caught by claims review or preflight, not by the research stage.

Pushed the 12 round-2 lead entries to the console from qualifier wording (r2_overrides.json) before the fact-check ran and did not re-sync afterwards; unverified phrases (Facebook lead form, Cordelia registered 12 Oct) remain in that text.
Did not notice for two rounds that found_in came back empty (10/10 in round 1, 3/12 in round 2 including both A leads), so source attribution had to be reconstructed.
Ran 12 qualifiers and 6 scouts in parallel on one shared WebSearch quota; the two A leads were graded with no web search at all.
Did not restate the operator's own 17 Oct stop rule when round 2 was requested, and did not reuse round 1's near-miss lists or its RERA-token join advice.
Treated the older Apify pool's 'A' grades as usable input; all five real-estate A rows downgraded on the browser re-check.
open_questions: Will any of the 9 contacted leads reply, and does reply rate differ by grade, hunger tier, source or channel lane? (Wave-2 WhatsApp templates were scheduled for 15:30 IST, outcome unknown at the time of this analysis.)
Is the Cordelia RERA approval of 12 Oct real? The R1 scout and R2 qualifier read it from GujRERA, the fact-check could not verify it; one direct API call would settle it.
Does a personal or free-mail inbox (Pride via the RERA Gmail) get read more than shared role inboxes? So far n=1 (page open + video play) and possibly a team visit.
Does 'WhatsApp path observed' (Pride, Brij, NB, Swagat, one Space Age ad) predict response better than 'unknown' (Great Spaces, Parshwanath, Elenza)?
Were the 22 R2 candidates that were never qualified weaker than the 12 that were, or only lower on the sourceCount + email score?

Is real-estate the right segment, given how many developers with websites already run a CRM or chatbot, versus the clinics and coaching rows in the 14 Oct Apify pool (17 of 30 rows) that this campaign never tried?
What does a recurring Apify budget cost versus the weekly Claude limit, and when does the Apify monthly cap reset?
Does the phone-first lane (owner's team calls) beat email-first for the 16 held-back phone-only click-to-WhatsApp advertisers?

headline: In 4 days, 12 real-lead emails reached 11 inboxes (1 bounce) and 3 cold WhatsApp templates reached 0 people, with zero replies and zero real demo taps. Our own monitoring produced more false "engagement" (6 of 8 signals were our own tests or link scanners) than real signals. The approval gate works and was never bypassed, but it costs about 2 owner codes per lead. Nobody or nothing reads email replies or STOP requests, and sends scheduled for later have no machine-enforced checks. Next campaign: keep email as the main channel, treat cold WhatsApp as a capped experiment with a coded stop-loss, make inbound email machine-readable, and replace per-send hand-waving with a no-model executor plus batch approval.

lessons.lesson: Cold WhatsApp MARKETING templates to business-published numbers did not deliver at all; owner-number tests prove rendering, not deliverability.
lessons.evidence: events.jsonl + memory.md AE: Brij template 15:09 IST accepted, Meta failed it ~5 s later with 131049; NB 15:39 failed 131026 (number cannot receive); Elenza 16:35 never got any status in 16+ h. The only 'delivered' sends were the owner's and boss's own numbers (XG72K, KR2AC; boss number READ 16:50). The 14 Oct research (AGENTIC_SALES_BLUEPRINT.md line 9, research_raw line ~765) had predicted this. The owner continued to NB 3 minutes after hearing of the Brij failure (agent had advised holding the rest), and for wave 2 chose to send to all 4 although the round-2 scouts wrote 'Do NOT cold-template' on several numbers (_research_raw_r2.json contact notes).
lessons.do_next_time: Make email the primary channel and the lead-initiated wa.me demo button the WhatsApp route. If the owner still wants cold templates: (1) write the success criterion before sending (e.g. 'at least 1 of the first 3 delivered'), (2) code a circuit breaker in the sender so that 2 failures with 131049/131026/no-status after 10 min stop the rest of that wave automatically and post the Meta phone quality rating, (3) never read an own-number test as a delivery forecast, (4) prefer a human 1:1 message from the company line for phone-only leads.

lessons.lesson: Email-then-WhatsApp sequencing was inconsistent and the pre-announcement in the wave-2 email promises something the cold template cannot guarantee.
lessons.evidence: Wave 1: Brij and NB WhatsApp went first (15:09, 15:39) and the emails 55-80 min later (16:29, 16:34); Elenza email 16:35:04 and WhatsApp 16:35:18, the bounce arrived 61 s later (sends.jsonl). Wave 2: emails 14:07:33-14:09:18, WhatsApp planned 15:30 (about 80-83 min) although the recipient-lens QA (_page_qa_r2.json, _page_qa_r2_pass2.json) said 3-4 h, skip WhatsApp if the lead opened/replied/wrote stop, and send email only when the number is not labelled WhatsApp (Great Spaces, Parshwanath). The v3 emails say 'Later today we will also send this same note on WhatsApp ... reply stop' (campaign1_v3/email_greatspaces.txt).
lessons.do_next_time: One fixed order: email first; WhatsApp only to leads whose number is labelled WhatsApp by the business, with a gap long enough for a human to read the 'stop' replies (3 h or more), and only if the engagement check shows no reply/tap/stop. Do not write 'we will also WhatsApp you' in the email unless the WhatsApp is conditional in code; otherwise say nothing about it. A broken promise (template fails) is worse than silence.

lessons.lesson: Email deliverability was assumed, not measured: 'delivered' is not inbox, one published address bounced, and sender authentication and a seed-inbox test were never recorded.
lessons.evidence: Elenza's site-published sales address bounced 61 s after send (events.jsonl 16:35:04 -> 16:36:05; suppression.txt). Round-1 had no MX check; round 2 added nslookup and caught Swarna (no MX) and SuperCITY (CAMPAIGN_PLAYBOOK 4). memory.md section 3: 'SPF/DKIM/DMARC status not verified'; the planned inbox-placement test (memory S) and the 'SPF/DKIM check before sending' (assistant 16 Oct 04:50Z) have no result anywhere; grep of the transcript finds no DMARC/SPF check of the sender domain. Research (research_raw_2026-10-14.json line ~761) said: dedicated subdomain, DMARC p=none, Gmail Postmaster, pause on complaints; actual sends use the main domain with a personal-name From mailbox. 0 genuine opens/clicks by any lead in 3 days, so 'not read' cannot be told from 'in spam'.
lessons.do_next_time: Add a preflight gate to propose.py: syntax + MX per address, sender-domain SPF/DKIM/DMARC check, hosted assets HEAD (already exists), and a seed test to 3 own mailboxes (Gmail, Outlook/Yahoo, a Zoho/Workspace) with a note on inbox vs promotions vs spam before wave 1. Move cold mail to a dedicated subdomain with a neutral From (not a staff name) before scaling past about 20 leads, and set a bounce/complaint stop rule (any complaint pauses the wave).

lessons.lesson: Inbound email is a blind spot: replies, STOP requests and unsubscribes go to mailboxes that neither the agent nor any automation reads.
lessons.evidence: send_email.py line 239 sets List-Unsubscribe to a mailto of the personal-name From address (no HTTPS one-click). The first-touch emails to Brij, NB and Elenza (codes NRQ8J, UHJG5, 9SA3V) had no Reply-To, so replies go to that personal mailbox; from Pride onward Reply-To is the shared info@ mailbox (owner_messages/*.txt). The wave-2 email promises 'reply stop to this email and we will not send it', and on 19 Oct 13:01 and 14:13 IST the operator asked the owner's team to watch info@ ('jo main nahi padh sakta'); no confirmation is recorded. The 'skip WhatsApp if the lead replied' rule cannot see email replies. Suppression for email stop is manual (suppress.py).
lessons.do_next_time: Before any send that promises an email opt-out, make inbound readable by machine: check whether Resend inbound (email.received webhook, same /hooks endpoint pattern as the existing resend hook) is available on the plan, else a plain-script IMAP poll of the Reply-To mailbox, writing email_reply entries to the console, auto-adding STOP/unsubscribe wording to suppression and alerting the owner. Replace the mailto List-Unsubscribe with an HTTPS one-click endpoint that writes suppression. Until then name one human and log their check before each WhatsApp slot.

lessons.lesson: The OK-code gate is sound (never bypassed) but costs about 2 codes per lead and the owner's reading time dominates; use batch approval of a template plus a variable table, not a weaker gate.
lessons.evidence: events.jsonl: 28 proposals created, 20 consumed, 4 wasted (9CZ37 had the owner's name, N2K53 superseded, WX85U burnt by a BSP /app failure, HNDWP expired unsent), 4 approved-held. Median proposal->send 10.2 min (n=20); wave-2 batch: 8 proposals 12:59 IST, emails sent 14:07-14:09 (68-70 min, approvals decided 08:37-08:38Z per heartbeat.log). 19 real-lead codes for 9 leads (2.1/lead) = about 60 codes for a 30-lead campaign. On 16 Oct the owner typed 'send' in chat three times and wrote 'time waste' ('karde send mujhe' 16:02 -> sent 16:20 IST) because a chat 'send' is not an approval; he asked for ONE code and was told no (memory 16 Oct). A chat-token workaround was refused as Security Weaken and reverted. Pride: instruction 16 Oct 16:44 IST, proposal HNDWP 16:51, OK missing, expired 04:51 IST, sent 17 Oct 10:05 (about 17 h). 52 owner_notify messages on 15-16 Oct (counters.json) caused the credit complaint that created quiet mode.
lessons.do_next_time: Start every wave with one sentence: 'Chat words are not approval; send OK CODE from your own WhatsApp'. Build CRM batch approval: one wave code that binds a list of exact action hashes, shown as one message (approved template text once + a per-lead table of variables, recipient, subject), single use, 12 h expiry, CRM-minted. Optionally evaluate an owner-authenticated Approve button in the console (owner login + CSRF, not the agent's API key), but treat it as a security change needing the owner's explicit decision and an independent review. Never mint approvals from the agent side. Create proposals only after the final copy (lesson from 3 burnt template codes) and ask for OK early in the day.

lessons.lesson: Sends that are approved but intentionally held have no machine state, so the scheduling and the pre-send checks live in the operator's head and the heartbeat wastes runs.
lessons.evidence: Wave-2 WhatsApp jobs (wave2_jobs_wa.json) are just 'campaign_send.py send <key> --approval CODE' with a 120 s gap; the engagement check (skip replied/tapped/stop) is a manual step planned for 15:30. heartbeat_check.py treats every approved-unused code as WORK, so the desktop heartbeat woke at 08:39Z, 08:54Z and 09:09Z only to decide 'not executing' (heartbeat.log). The 15:30 send depends on the attended chat's background waiter staying alive. 16 Oct 15:11 IST race: unattended heartbeat told the owner 'lead got nothing' for a send that had happened (memory 'Heartbeat race'); fast lane also answered 'not sent'. The watcher already retries when the window is closed (3ZFSQ blocked 25 s before 09:30 on 19 Oct).
lessons.do_next_time: Build a no-model executor (plain Python, so the Claude classifier is not involved) that reads a job file with not_before, hold flag and approved code, and enforces in code: window, weekday/festival calendar, suppression, ignore list, lead has no reply/tap/stop/email-reply, page and video return 200, ad-recheck stamp from today, 2-minute gap, status read at +60 s, circuit breaker on repeated failures, then writes a verified result line. Teach heartbeat_check.py a 'held-until' state so held codes do not wake it. Only one actor may report send state, and only from sends.jsonl + crm.py approval.

lessons.lesson: Monitoring misread machine and our-own traffic as lead interest: 6 of the 8 signals seen in 4 days were false, and the level logic still counts any non-bot page GET as 'engaged'.
lessons.evidence: False: owner's own test-email click made Brij look engaged (ignore window 16 Oct 10:50-10:58Z); boss test number made Pride look 'Delivered' (fixed by last-4 matching); Rivanta 'opened' 30 s after send and NB 'opened' 20 s after delivery (memory 19 Oct); Great Spaces 'page opened 2x' and a Resend click 6 s after send (scanner; thresholds set to 30 s page / 60 s click from that single case, engagement_sync.py lines 135, 519); Pride card HOT from the team's 0674 demo test at 10:50-10:52 IST, 25 min after the follow-up was sent (ignore window added after the fact). Unverified-real: Brij page open 17 Oct 09:02 IST, Pride visit+video play 19 Oct 09:10 IST (may also be team). level_of (engagement_sync.py lines 171-189): any non-bot page open = engaged, any cta click or handoff = hot. Email event times were 'first seen' times until the webhook (19 Oct).
lessons.do_next_time: (1) Confidence levels: 'hot' only for a reply or demo from a number matched to the lead, anything else shows as 'possible' with the reason. (2) Count a page visit only if a JS dwell beacon (about 5 s visible plus a scroll/touch) fires; a bare GET is 'fetched'. (3) Email opens never count; clicks count only after 60 s and with a later page event. (4) Keep scanner windows but log every dropped event so thresholds can be re-fitted, they come from n=1. (5) Before a wave, register every team phone/email/browser in DEMO_TEST_NUMBERS and engagement_ignore.json, and tell the team to test with the [Test] email to the owner's own address (the 3XJ7Z route), not lead links; consider a '?src=team' flag that suppresses beacons. (6) Add the six misreads as regression tests in test_engagement_sync.py.

lessons.lesson: Nobody is guaranteed to see a hot reply in time: owner-quiet mode removes all push alerts, the heartbeat only runs when the PC and app are on, and the console is passive.
lessons.evidence: OWNER_QUIET suppresses WhatsApp and email to the owner (file text); fast lane DOWN in every heartbeat.log line since 16 Oct; heartbeat.log has no line for Sun 18 Oct and none between 17 Oct 17:53 IST and 19 Oct 09:10 IST (about 39 h); the heartbeat needs the PC on with the Claude app open (memory 15 Oct). Only the VPS-side demo responder and the 5-minute engagement cron run 24/7, and they write to the console without alerting. The VPS reboot of 17 Oct 11:14-11:37 IST (pages, webhooks and console down) was found by the owner ('crm bnad he'), not by monitoring. The site footer included on every landing page shows the boss's personal number (memory 16 Oct number correction), so a lead could call him with no briefing.
lessons.do_next_time: Write a watch matrix into the playbook and the wave checklist: agent (attended chat) = sends, +60 s status read, console check every 30 min during a wave; VPS cron = engagement and email webhooks; named human = info@ mailbox and the company phone line; owner = console glance at day start and end. Add a free alert path for four events only (lead reply, demo 'Yes/person', STOP/complaint, bounce spike): an email from the console server to the owner's own inbox or a Telegram bot, exempt from quiet mode and rate-limited. Add an external uptime check (different network) on one landing page and the webhook route; do not start a wave if it is red. Brief the boss before the wave about calls from the footer number.

lessons.lesson: Timing: the 09:30-19:00 window is clock-only, the first plausible reactions came at the next working morning, and the QA's ideal slot was missed because approval took over an hour.
lessons.evidence: config.json send_window_ist 09:30-19:00, no weekday or festival logic (Pride email Sat 17 Oct 10:05). Brij email Fri 16:29 -> page open Sat 09:02 IST (about 16.5 h); Pride email Sat 10:05 -> visit Mon 09:10 IST (about 47 h). Recipient QA: email 10:30-11:30 weekday, WhatsApp 3-4 h later; actual wave 2 emails 14:07-14:09 (approval latency 68 min) and WhatsApp 15:30. Rivanta notes: weekdays only, stop touches by about 5 Nov, Diwali about 8 Nov (memory 19 Oct). Follow-ups Brij/NB/Pride went on Mon 19 Oct, 3 days after the first mail.
lessons.do_next_time: Make the executor weekday-only with a festival block list, and plan the morning: assets and copy frozen the evening before, approvals requested by 10:00 for a 10:30 send, WhatsApp (if any) no earlier than 3 h later and before 17:30. Keep the code-level window. Treat the 'next working morning' pattern as a hypothesis (n=2) and log first-reaction time per lead to fit the slot.

lessons.lesson: Copy and template wording must be decided against the sales goal before the first send: video-first v1 went out in half of the lead emails, and the fixed WhatsApp template still carries a claim the email rules forbid.
lessons.evidence: Of 12 lead emails, 6 were v1 ('A short video for X', video-first: Brij, NB, Elenza, Pride, Rivanta first touches and Brij's follow-up), 2 were v2f (offer-first 'Automatic WhatsApp replies for X enquiries': NB, Pride follow-ups), 4 were v3 (wave 2). The owner caught the mismatch on 19 Oct 09:34 IST ('hume whatsapp automation bechna he, video nahi'). v1->v2: outcome subject + 'what we do' paragraph first, no 'your ads', no 'free/instant' (playbook 12e). v2->v3 (fact-check + recipient QA): lead-specific observation first, 'under 40 seconds', project name first in subject (phone inbox cuts about 40 chars), address-source line moved to the footer, opt-out line. QA items still open: 'from our own number' for a +1 555 number (finding 9) and the Parshwanath 'WhatsApp' premise. The approved WA template (owner_messages/9BNDD.txt) says 'We saw your ads for {{2}}' and uses {{2}} twice, which forced the Space Age compromise; template approval took about 20 min (created 13:39 IST 16 Oct, APPROVED by about 14:00).
lessons.do_next_time: Write one 'goal sentence' per campaign and make the copy builder lint against it (subject must state the outcome, no asset-first subjects, no 'your ads', 'free', 'instant', staff names). Since Meta approved in about 20 min, submit a v2 template whenever the copy rules change, with separate variables for 'what we saw' and 'what we made' and wording true for the weakest-evidence lead. Run the recipient-lens QA on emails AND the WhatsApp template text before codes are requested, and state in the email who the +1 sender is ('IV Infotech, verified WhatsApp Business number').

mistakes_we_made: Shipped first-touch emails with a personal-name From mailbox, no Reply-To on the first three (NRQ8J, UHJG5, 9SA3V) and a List-Unsubscribe mailto to that same unread mailbox; SPF/DKIM/DMARC and the seed inbox test were planned (memory S, assistant 16 Oct 04:50Z) but never recorded, and the dedicated-subdomain advice from the 14 Oct research was not followed.

Round 1 emails were not MX-checked or validated; Elenza's published address bounced within 61 s and the same lead's WhatsApp went out 14 s after the email, before the bounce was known. The MX check was only added in round 2.

Video-first v1 subject/copy went into 6 of 12 lead emails even though the operator's own 16 Oct strategy (memory Q) said the angle was the outcome; the owner, not QA or the operator, caught it on 19 Oct.

Operators gave contradictory send-state reports within minutes on 16 Oct: the desktop heartbeat said 'lead got nothing' for a send that had happened and the fast lane said 'not sent'; the truth was 'sent but not delivered (131049)'. Three workers watching the same approvals is a design flaw, the prompt rules are only a patch.

Wasted approval codes and owner messages: 9CZ37 carried the owner's name, N2K53 superseded, WX85U consumed before the BSP app-id read failed (fixed to read-before-consume), HNDWP (Pride) had an overstated hook and expired unsent; four template-create requests of about 1.4-1.6k chars each for one template.

Built the scanner filter (30 s page / 60 s click) from a single observation (Great Spaces, 6 s) and left level_of counting any non-bot page GET as engaged; the team-test and boss-test misattributions were each fixed only after they had already shown wrong cards.

Did not make 'held' a state: approved WhatsApp codes were left for the heartbeat to re-evaluate, producing three empty wake-ups in 30 min, and the engagement gate before the 15:30 send exists only as an intention.
Relied on people to watch the info@ mailbox for 'stop' replies without a confirmation that anyone did, while the email text promises an opt-out before the WhatsApp slot.
No external uptime monitor: the 23-minute VPS reboot on 17 Oct took down the landing pages linked from live emails, the console and the webhook, and was discovered by the owner.
numbers: Real-lead sends so far (sends.jsonl): 12 emails (11 delivered, 1 hard bounce) to 9 distinct addresses, 3 cold WhatsApp templates (0 delivered: 131049, 131026, no status). 4 more cold templates held for 15:30 IST (outcome unknown at time of writing).

Replies from leads: 0. Demo-button taps by leads: 0 (only the team's 0674 test). Plausible real page visits: 2 (Brij 17 Oct 09:02 IST, Pride 19 Oct 09:10 IST), both unverified. Source: memory.md journal 17-19 Oct.

Email copy mix of 12 lead emails: v1 video-first 6, v2f offer-first follow-up 2, v3 4 (sends.jsonl subjects).

open_questions: Outcome of the 15:30 IST wave-2 WhatsApp round: how many of the 4 deliver, and did Meta's phone number quality rating or messaging tier move after 3 + 4 cold templates? Nobody re-reads the quality rating after sends today.

Does anyone read the shared Reply-To mailbox and the personal-name From mailbox, and has any lead already replied or sent STOP by email? Does Resend inbound exist on this plan or must it be an IMAP poll?
Are our emails landing in inbox, promotions or spam? SPF/DKIM/DMARC status of the sending domain and a seed-inbox result are unknown; zero genuine opens/clicks cannot be explained either way.
Were Brij's 17 Oct 09:02 visit and Pride's 19 Oct 09:10 visit and video play the leads or the team?
Would a lead-initiated route (wa.me button in the email) ever convert for this segment? 0 taps in 9 leads so far, n is too small to decide.
Is the 'next working morning, 09:00-09:10 IST' first-reaction pattern real (n=2)? Needs per-lead first-reaction times from wave 2 and 3.
Would the owner accept an owner-authenticated console Approve button or CRM batch approval, given the earlier agent-minted token was refused as a security weakening?
Does the pre-announcement in the wave-2 email ('Later today we will also send this on WhatsApp') change reply or opt-out behaviour, or WhatsApp delivery? Not testable without an A/B.

headline: Five QA runs plus one pre-build fact-check produced 142 findings (55 major or high), and the same few classes kept coming back: unverified statements about the lead's ads, defaults and undecided owner claims shipped as fact (free, calendar, forms), reseller and third-party-brand handling, the pitch selling "a video" instead of WhatsApp automation, and long-name layout collisions. Almost all were catchable earlier and cheaper by a claims ledger, typed per-lead truth fields with no defaults, lints that run on every surface, and a gate that blocks open owner decisions. The costly leftovers are the baked voice-over (10 videos) and the frozen WhatsApp template body, which cannot be corrected per lead, plus five live wave-1 pages that were never rebuilt after the template fixes.

lessons.lesson: Write a claims ledger before the first asset and make it cover every surface (page, email, WhatsApp template body, voice text, video on-screen text, banner image), because one wrong claim lived in up to seven places and each QA pass found it in a different one.
lessons.evidence: HOW IN: wave-1 copy was written for click-to-WhatsApp leads and reused as defaults. The 'your ads / ads that open a WhatsApp chat' family sits in: template H1 (pass-2 claims major, _page_qa_r2_pass2.json), h3 'A buyer taps your WhatsApp ad' and FAQ 'the number your ads point to' (pass 1, _page_qa_r2.json), hero sender-line default, voice lines 1-2 (master_voice_en_v2.txt), on-screen headline (agent/video/master_video.html:151), template body 'We saw your ads for {{2}}' (wave1_template_en_spec.json) and the sent Brij/NB/Elenza emails ('Your Sandalwood ads open a WhatsApp chat'). CAUGHT BY: QA v1 claims lens had to build the S/C/X ledger itself at the end (17 rows, _page_qa_v1.json); the r2 QA context only banned 'your ads' in the EMAIL (lead-page-qa-r2.js CONTEXT), so the page H1 passed pass 1 and surfaced in pass 2 (13 majors in pass 1, still 11 in pass 2). KB proof_points.md was already a prose ledger (bans 'instant', says repeat 'free' only if the owner re-confirms) but nothing in the build reads it.
lessons.do_next_time: EARLIER GATE (cost: ~1 hour once per campaign, then free): create agent/claims/ledger.json with one row per claim: id, wording, allowed surfaces, evidence type (service fact confirmed by owner / observed ad ID / lead's own page), evidence ref, owner-decision status, banned variants. build_pages.py, build_email_drafts.py, the template spec and the voice script must pull wording from ledger ids; a lint greps every built artifact and the voice text for banned variants. Write QA rules as 'on ALL surfaces', and give pass 2 the ledger plus a diff of what pass 1 changed.

lessons.lesson: Run the per-lead fact-check BEFORE building and store its output as typed truth fields (not prose), keep fact-checkers to facts and a do-not-claim list, and include the template-level global sentences in scope.
lessons.evidence: wave2-fact-check: 4 agents, ~9 min (06:38Z launch, transcript), 32 problems (9/8/7/8, _wave2_factcheck.json); 4 of 4 draft hooks needed correction (Aaroham: 'book a site visit' is Novarra's wording; Swagat: only 2 of 3 ads have the WhatsApp button and those two never name Cilantra; Parshwanath: 'lead form' unverified, FB.ME destination unknown; Space Age: 'only phone numbers' incomplete). Wave 1 had no such step: QA v1 called chips 'unverified guesses' (pride 3/4 BHK, brij 3/4, nb 4/5, elenza 2 BHK/Shop) and caught Elenza 'Shop' is not a BHK. Research output itself contradicted itself: Parshwanath best_angle says 'we answer every Facebook lead-form enquiry' while its own hypotheses say lead form NOT verified; r2 said Cordelia 'RERA-registered 12 Oct', fact-check could not verify (_research_raw_r2.json). Prices: Swagat portals range 72.6 lakh to 2.65 Cr, Parshwanath 25.7 to 55 lakh, so no price is printed anywhere. The fact-check also caused one error: it suggested chip 'Other size' for a 2-BHK-only project (recipient lens pass 1). Its output was hand-copied into leads.json, so Parshwanath video (rendered 12:24) says 'Other size' while the page (leads.json 12:37) says 'Tell me more' (pass 2).
lessons.do_next_time: EARLIER GATE: make the qualifier/fact-check emit required fields per lead (project_name_exact + collision list, entity_type developer/reseller/broker, unit labels verbatim with type BHK/plot/villa/shop, ads: count, CTA per ad ID, destination known?, start date, advertiser_page_is_lead's_own_page, contact source URL, price printed? never, trademark notice, do_not_claim[], as_of date). Generate hooks only from observed fields, never from hypotheses. Fact-checker returns facts only; one writer produces copy under the ledger. Auto-import the JSON into leads.json instead of retyping. Run a separate one-time claims review of the template's global sentences (H1, h3, FAQ), because per-lead checks cannot see them.

lessons.lesson: A factual slot must never have a default value: required truth fields should fail the build when missing, because defaults silently turned wave-1 assumptions into claims about wave-2 leads.
lessons.evidence: HOW IN: build_pages.py falls back to 'runs ads that open a WhatsApp chat' when ads_phrase is absent, and build_email_drafts.py defaults to 'We saw your ads for %s'. Swagat had no ads_phrase, so its hero line said all ads open WhatsApp when only 2 of 3 do (pass-1 claims major). Rivanta: the 19 Oct preflight fixed the hook ('several ways to enquire', only one ad has a WhatsApp button) but not the default sender line; the built page agent/state/site_dist/templates/campaign/lead_rivanta.html (09:28) still says 'Rivanta Heritage runs ads that open a WhatsApp chat', and the Rivanta email went out 09:32. CAUGHT BY: pass-1 claims lens (Swagat); nobody (Rivanta).
lessons.do_next_time: EARLIER GATE (a 10-line code change): remove every default for ads_phrase, ads_seen, hook, email_saw, unit chips and demo_free; build_pages.py and build_email_drafts.py raise an error naming the lead and the field. Add the field ads_owner_verified (true only when the advertiser page is linked from the lead's own site); 'your ads' is allowed only when true, else 'ads for X'. After fixing a claim in one slot, grep the built file for the old wording before sending.

lessons.lesson: Open owner decisions must gate the build, and the voice-over may contain no undecided claim, because 'free', calendar and forms went live as defaults while memory still listed them as open.
lessons.evidence: HOW IN: leads.json has demo_free: True with _flags_note 'confirm before the first send'; KB proof_points.md rule 3 says repeat 'free' only if the owner re-confirms; memory.md (AA, AB) and playbook line 86 still list 'is the demo free / what does Yes send' as open on 19 Oct; the transcript shows no owner answer on 'free' (only 'badiya, pasand aaya' after his own test, 16 Oct 09:28Z). RESULT: voice line 'The demo is free, no obligation' is in all 10 renders (9 lead videos + SAMPLE), ' Free.' is on all 9 built pages. CAUGHT BY: video QA v1 (forms claim, 'free' ambiguous, 2 high) and v2 (free + 'Site visits land on your calendar', 2 high). The calendar line was copied from QA-v1's own fix suggestion without checking the service (v2 claims lens), so reviewer suggestions are as untrusted as our own copy.
lessons.do_next_time: EARLIER GATE: decisions register (agent/claims/decisions.json: id, question, owner answer, date). Any ledger row that depends on an open decision is rendered neutral by the build (e.g. 'A demo for X', no calendar/forms sentence) and the build refuses to publish a surface that needs the answer. Ask the owner the 4-5 open questions in ONE message before the first voice take instead of discovering them in two video QA rounds. Verify any reviewer-suggested feature line against the service-facts register before adopting it.

lessons.lesson: Know exactly what each surface can personalise and put every lead-specific or undecided claim on the cheapest surface to change, because the voice-over and the approved WhatsApp template body are effectively frozen.
lessons.evidence: CAN: video on-screen slots project, city, time, bhk1, bhk2 (render_master.py args) plus headline strings in master_video.html (edit and re-render, ~5 min each); page and email fields in leads.json (rebuild plus deploy, minutes); WhatsApp template only {{1}} greeting, {{2}} project (used twice), header video link chosen at send time (no re-approval), URL-button suffix (slug). CANNOT: one MP3 serves every lead and says nothing lead-specific; any spoken change means a new ElevenLabs take made by the owner in the web UI (library voices are not available through the free API), build_timeline.py, then re-render all 10 videos (~50 min at ~5 min each) and redeploy pages; any template body change needs a new Meta template (iv_en_realestate_demo_v1 was created 13:39 IST on 16 Oct and approved within about 20 min, but plan for hours to a day). Frozen text today: voice 'Every enquiry from your ads gets', 'your WhatsApp ads', 'Your people join anytime', 'free'; template 'We saw your ads for {{2}}', 'next developer' (wrong for a reseller). Pass-2 claims lens called the voice untrue for Great Spaces and Parshwanath; owner accepted 'for now' (memory.md 242). Re-record backlog since 16 Oct (3 days): say what the demo is, 'a person from your team can join the chat', 'can get', 'for buyers who agree', one outcome line, drop 'free' if declined, plus 'your WhatsApp ads' from pass 2. Four MP3s were made 9-16 Oct; v1 to v2 took 36 min (05:57Z to 06:33Z).
lessons.do_next_time: Rule: audio carries only claims true for ALL leads and decided by the owner (benefit, steps, 'can'); everything lead-specific or undecided ('your ads', 'free', project name) goes on-screen in editable HTML or into the page/email. Keep one separate template per lead class (developer with verified ads / reseller / unverified ad owner) so {{2}} and 'your ads' are always true; test template params used twice against each class. Bundle voice fixes only from the decisions register, and re-record before the first send, not after nine videos exist.

lessons.lesson: Add an offer-alignment check ('does this message sell what we sell, and what is the single ask?') to every QA lens set, because the owner, not QA, caught that six sent emails sold 'a short video'.
lessons.evidence: sends.jsonl: subjects 'A short video for X' went to Brij (16 Oct), NB, Elenza (bounced), Pride (17 Oct), Rivanta (19 Oct 09:32) plus 'Following up: short video for BRIJ Sandalwood' (19 Oct 09:30): six emails. Owner message 19 Oct 04:04Z (09:34 IST), two minutes after the Rivanta send: 'we sell WhatsApp automation, the video only explains it'; the operator agreed. No lens (comprehension, claims, visual, recipient, muted, ad-hoc preflight) ever tested this; the Rivanta preflight with three lenses, which changed hook, chips and poster frame, left the subject untouched. The same shape recurs in the video: 'Same enquiry. Reply in a minute.' did not say what the product was until 13 s (video QA v1 muted lens, high).
lessons.do_next_time: EARLIER GATE (one sentence, zero tokens): store a one-line offer and ask in the campaign file ('automatic WhatsApp replies for enquiry ads; ask: watch 40 s / try the demo'). Checks: subject names the outcome in the lead's words (not 'a video'); first paragraph says what we do before what we made; page H1 and the first 8 s of the video state the product; template body leads with the product. Add 'offer alignment' as a fourth lens and require it on the first email of each new copy version.

lessons.lesson: Model resellers and third-party brands as a schema variant (advertises versus made_for, entity_type, trademark rule), because one 'project' slot made everything lead-facing read as made for a developer who is not the recipient.
lessons.evidence: Fact-check flagged reseller and the developer's trademark notice BEFORE the build (spaceage problems 1-2, _wave2_factcheck.json), yet the video was first rendered as 'Arvind Sensora' (render_r2.log), then re-rendered as space_age_consultants at 12:39 (2 of 6 wave-2 renders were rework, ~10 min). Pass-1 claims majors: eyebrow/title/og, email banner and video chat header 'Arvind Sensora online' imitated the developer's voice; non-affiliation only in the last footer paragraph; email 'We help real-estate developers' wrong for a consultancy. lessons.lesson: Make the owner approval show the claims, not just the text: the approval hash covers email or template text only, so claims in the video, page and banner are approved by nobody, and facts about live ads decay in days.

Facts decay: wave-2 ads are 1-16 days old (Sensora WhatsApp ad since 18 Oct); the send-day Ad Library recheck took 30 s and returned 4 of 4 send_as_is. QA warned in three separate outputs (_page_qa_v1 claims #1, r2 recipient, r2 pass2 recipient) that a same-day cold marketing template to unlabeled numbers risks opt-in blocks; wave 1 then saw Brij 131049, NB 131026, Elenza no status. Decision stayed with the owner, but the warning materialised.
lessons.do_next_time: EARLIER GATE: propose.py appends, to every approval message, the ledger ids used, the truth-sheet as_of time, the QA verdict with open findings, and the sha256 of header video, banner and page build; a send is refused if any hash differs or as_of is older than 24 h unless the Ad Library recheck is re-run. Per lead, record whether the number is labelled WhatsApp or only a call line, and show that to the owner next to the code.

lessons.lesson: PRE-BUILD CHECKLIST (do these in order before generating any page, video, email or template for a campaign or a lead).
lessons.evidence: Derived from the five QA runs (142 findings), the wave-2 fact-check (32 problems) and the owner corrections (offer, personal number, free). Wave-2 timeline shows it fits: request 06:33Z, fact-check 06:38Z, QA pass 1 06:59Z, pass 2 07:11Z, deployed 07:30Z (~57 min), so front-loading the data step does not slow the campaign.
lessons.do_next_time: 1) Campaign once: one-line offer and ask; service-facts register (what is confirmed: demo contents, forms, calendar, reminders, human takeover, timing 'about a minute' measured end to end); decisions register with every open item answered or rendered neutral; ledger.json built from KB proof_points. 2) Voice script and WhatsApp template body written ONLY from ledger rows true for all leads; no 'your ads', 'free', 'instant', 'gets', 'every', 'look after it', 'never share'. 3) Per lead truth sheet with source URL or ad ID and as_of date: exact project name and collision list (Aaroham vs Ashiana, Swagat Developers/Builders/SWAGATBUILDCON, Parshwanath Corporation Ltd is a different BSE company); entity_type, advertises vs made_for; unit labels verbatim and type (4B3HK stays 4B3HK, plots in sq yd, shop is not BHK, 2-BHK-only means no 'other size' chip); ads: count, CTA per ad ID, destination known?, start dates, ads_owner_verified; published contact and its source, labelled WhatsApp or call; no price anywhere (chips are sample answers); RERA wording 'scheduled' not 'registered', no possession dates; trademark/non-affiliation text; do_not_claim list. 4) Schema has no defaults for facts, display name <= 20 chars, hook <= 160 chars from observed fields only. 5) Build all slugs, run lint_all.py and the stress-name render, then QA lenses = claims, recipient, visual, offer alignment, with the ledger and truth sheet as ground truth and rules written for all surfaces.

lessons.lesson: PRE-SEND CHECKLIST (do these on the send day for every email and WhatsApp template, in order).
lessons.evidence: Derived from: send-day Ad Library recheck (30 s, 4 of 4 send_as_is), email-first ordering advice (QA recipient lens: email 10:30-11:30 IST, WhatsApp 3+ h later; owner chose 15:30 IST, ~80 min), Meta failures 131049/131026, scanner clicks 6 s after delivery (fixed in sync), the Rivanta default sender line, and the 'stop' email needing to reach suppression before the WhatsApp slot.
lessons.do_next_time: 1) Re-run the Ad Library recheck for every ad-dependent claim; if an ad type is gone, swap to the prepared fallback wording and rebuild page and email, or drop that lead's message. 2) Compare manifest hashes: live page, video, banner and header video equal the audited build (including wave-1 pages rebuilt after template fixes). 3) Run lint_all.py on the exact approved text; confirm no open decision is referenced. 4) Email: subject names the product and the project, preheader written explicitly, no staff names, no 'your ads' unless ads_owner_verified, address-source line true and in the footer, STOP line, the WhatsApp heads-up is certain and gives an exit, and the lead's 'stop' reply suppresses the WhatsApp before its slot. 5) WhatsApp: body true for this lead class and {{2}} true at both uses, number labelled WhatsApp or the opt-in risk accepted per lead in the approval message, skip any lead that replied, tapped or opened. 6) Approval message shows ledger ids, as_of time, QA verdict, hashes. 7) After the send: read the delivery status after ~1 min (131049/131026 mean not delivered), discard scanner-timed clicks, and log which claims each lead saw.

mistakes_we_made: Shipped 'free' as a default (leads.json demo_free: True) into the baked voice (10 renders) and 9 pages while KB proof_points rule 3 and the decisions list said it was not confirmed; the owner never answered it in chat.

Wrote the wave-1 email copy to sell 'a short video' and sent six emails with it before the owner pointed out, two minutes after the Rivanta send, that we sell WhatsApp automation; no QA lens tested offer alignment.

Used the boss's personal number as the WhatsApp and call number on four live pages (owner corrected 16 Oct 2026); the only code guard that exists for content is a one-number blacklist added after the fact.
Let factual fields have defaults ('runs ads that open a WhatsApp chat', 'We saw your ads for X'); Swagat got it by omission in pass 1, and Rivanta's page still carries it after the hook was fixed.

Hand-copied fact-check output into leads.json: introduced 'Other size' for a 2-BHK-only project, rendered the Space Age video as 'Arvind Sensora' before QA, and changed Parshwanath's chip 13 minutes after rendering its video (2 of 6 wave-2 renders were rework).
Added 'Site visits land on your calendar' to the video straight from a QA-v1 fix suggestion without checking the service had a calendar feature (video QA v2, high).
Scoped the QA 'never say your ads' rule to the email only, so the same claim passed pass 1 on the page H1, FAQ, video and template.
Did not apply pass-1's play-button fix and then changed poster_at to 17 s, so the play button hid the personalised chip row (pass 2, major).
Did not rebuild the five wave-1 pages after fixing the template, so they still carry claims that two QA passes removed from the wave-2 pages.
Left the three wave-2 gate scripts (fact-check, ad recheck, Rivanta preflight) outside the repo's agent/workflows/ folder.

Accepted that the shared voice says 'Every enquiry from your ads gets...' for Great Spaces and Parshwanath, which the pass-2 claims lens called untrue for those two, because re-recording was costly; the cost grew because the re-record list was left open for 3 days.

headline: Campaign 1 proved the machine, not the message. A 4-lead wave now takes about 56 minutes of agent time from the owner's "go" to ready-to-send (wave 1 took about 23 hours of wall-clock), and the safety gates no longer block anything. But 71 hours after the first send there are 0 replies and 0 button taps, cold WhatsApp templates delivered 0 of 3, and only 2 real page opens, so campaign 2 must be gated on what Day 3-5 shows. The shortest honest path is to prepare in parallel (research, fact-check, voice, a day-0 human checklist) and send a same-vertical wave in about 4 hours, or a new vertical in about 1.5-2 working days.

lessons.lesson: Reuse is the speed lever: with the master voice, Meta template and page template already built, wave 2 went from the owner's 'go' (12:03) to 'ready to send' (12:59) in 56 minutes of agent time. Wave 1 took about 23 hours wall-clock. The long poles are only what a human or Meta must do.

lessons.do_next_time: Same product and vertical: only add leads.json entries (playbook 12f recipe). New vertical: at T+0, in parallel with research, start the owner's voice take, the Mobbin design pack and the Meta template submission, because these are the only parts the agent cannot compress. Correct the playbook line 'render ~5 min each' to ~1.5 min each, ~6 min for four.

lessons.lesson: Speed to send is solved, speed to learn is not, so campaign 2 needs a learning gate. 71 hours after the first send (16 Oct 15:09 to 19 Oct 14:40) there are 0 replies, 0 button taps and 0 demos by a real lead, from 9 contacted leads. That sample is too small to compare Hungry vs Warm, which was the stated purpose.
lessons.evidence: sends.jsonl (15 real lead sends: 12 emails, 3 WhatsApp templates); memory.md entries 2026-10-17 09:05, 2026-10-19 (Pride hand-off) and 245; playbook section 5 (wave 2 only after the wave-1 reply rate is known); memory.md 234 (stop all touches by ~5 Nov, Diwali ~8 Nov, weekdays only).
lessons.do_next_time: Realistic timeline. Today (Mon 19 Oct): the 15:30 WhatsApp round. Thu 22 Oct: touch-2 for wave 2. By Mon 26 Oct: last notes and a read of the results. Tue 20 to Fri 23 Oct: campaign-2 prep that touches nobody (research 35-63 min, fact-check 9 min, script, owner voice). If replies are still 0, change the offer or message (human 1:1 first, a live demo number) rather than adding volume. Otherwise start after Diwali. Same-vertical wave about 4 h from go to first send; new vertical 1.5-2 working days.

lessons.lesson: Verify the pitch premise per lead before building, and keep lead-specific claims out of the fixed voice-over. The product is WhatsApp automation, but for 2 of 4 wave-2 leads the evidence does not show their ads open WhatsApp. Both QA passes flagged it, and it still ships in the video narration as 'owner-accepted' because fixing it needs a new ElevenLabs take.
lessons.evidence: _page_qa_r2.json and _page_qa_r2_pass2.json (claims lens): Great Spaces 'Book Now' destination unknown, Parshwanath fb.me with no WhatsApp entry point; _wave2_factcheck.json (9.3 min, 0.51M tokens) caught the wrong hook, '4B3HK' vs 4 BHK, 2-BHK-only project and the reseller; memory.md 242-243 (known issue: voice says 'your WhatsApp ads').
lessons.do_next_time: Make the scouts record per-ad CTA destination (WhatsApp / lead form / website / unknown) and a premise_proven flag, and rank lead-proven leads first. Run the fact-check on the top 6 before the owner picks. Record the next voice take premise-free ('every WhatsApp enquiry can get a reply'). Put per-lead facts only in captions, the page and the email, never in the audio.

lessons.lesson: Cold WhatsApp marketing templates did not deliver, though the research predicted it before anything was built: email delivered 11 of 12 and cold templates 0 of 3. Two days of WhatsApp-specific build (template, 84-test demo responder, engagement tracking) came before the first delivery test. Wave 2 repeats the same bet with 4 more templates today at 15:30, at the owner's choice.

lessons.do_next_time: Treat today's 4 wave-2 template results (read Meta status about 1 minute after each send) as the deciding data point and write the delivery rate into the playbook. If 0-1 of 4 deliver, drop cold templates and use email plus the wa.me button (lead-initiated, free window) plus a human 1:1 from a real phone. For any new campaign, send one cold probe to a non-owner number before building WhatsApp-specific assets.

lessons.lesson: Contactability is the narrowest funnel stage. Only 9 of 22 researched leads (41%) were actually contacted. The rest were blocked by language (5 Gujarati/mixed leads waiting for a voice take), no email route, no MX record, bounce risk, or low grade.
lessons.evidence: memory.md 240-241 (11 of 12 R2 leads had an email, Swarna had no MX, Nitya parked, 5 are wave-3 Gujarati); _research_raw_r2.json scouts (about 20 of ~150 Gujarat advertisers have their own site and email; GujRERA: 7 of 159 fresh promoters use a business email); Elenza bounced on 16 Oct (round 1 had no MX check); R1 warm/cold leads Beverlynn, Silver, Lotus, Trinetra, Somnath never sent.
lessons.do_next_time: Make email_mx_ok (nslookup -type=mx), email_source_url, a phone for a human call and the lead's language mandatory scout outputs. Stop the research workflow when N usable leads are reached (target_good). Do not rank a lead as sendable if its language has no voice or template yet.

lessons.lesson: A day-0 checklist for the things only a human can do would remove most of the idle waiting. The operator can already research, fact-check, build, render, QA, deploy, propose, send (after an OK code) and monitor alone. Everything else is a person.
lessons.evidence: CLAUDE.md human gates; memory.md and playbook: 28 OK-code proposals; ElevenLabs MP3 by the owner (2 takes on 16 Oct; Gujarati clips pending since 17 Oct); Apify hard limit since 15 Oct (still blocked 19 Oct); secrets only via set_vps_secret.ps1 (Resend whsec saved a file path on the first try, 19 Oct 11:05); the allow-rule for vps_run.sh added by the owner 15 Oct 17:08-17:10; 'deploy it' 12:57; replies and STOP go to info@ which the agent cannot read; the Pride call was made by the owner's team; free demo, pricing and claims are owner decisions.
lessons.do_next_time: Day-0 message to the owner (one list): (1) Apify credit, (2) voice recording slot if the vertical or language is new, (3) who watches the info@ mailbox and a neutral From address (From is still a personal-name address, Reply-To is info@), (4) confirm the vps_run.sh rule exists, (5) fixed daily send hour, (6) team test phones and IPs for the ignore list, (7) who makes human calls, (8) open claim decisions (is the demo free, what does 'Yes' send), (9) secrets via the hidden prompt only.

lessons.lesson: The OK-code gate is cheap when batched and scheduled and costly when ad hoc. Eight proposals were created in 16 seconds and approved in about 90 seconds once the owner arrived, but he arrived 68 minutes later. Only the first use cost 23 minutes of friction. 8 of the 28 codes were wasted or are still waiting.
lessons.evidence: proposals.jsonl (wave 2: 12:59:33-49 created; sends.jsonl 14:07:33-14:09:18); wave 1 OK latency 5-10 min (16:24:42 to 16:35:18); Rivanta 95 s; NB/Pride follow-ups 14 min; owner messages 16 Oct 15:57, 16:02, 16:12, 16:18, 16:19 ('bhai me bol raha hu bhejde'), actual send 16:20:23 because chat text is not an approval; wasted: 9CZ37 and N2K53 (wording changed), WX85U (burnt by a provider failure), HNDWP (expired unsent after 12 h); pending: 9BNDD, 7A45D, U95HA, UY4VY.
lessons.do_next_time: Agree one daily send hour with the owner (he asked to be present: 'UNHE 3.30 KO BHEJO TAKI KOI ISSUE AYE TO ME YAHA HU'). Create the whole batch of proposals and show ONE consolidated message 10 minutes before it, with wording frozen (any change means a new code). Use the watcher for send window and gaps. A server-side batch-approval build is not worth it at about 90 seconds of owner time per 8 sends.

lessons.lesson: Monitoring is noisy, and only a few signals are real: a human page visit well after the send, a video play, a button tap or a reply. Fake signals came from link scanners, mail-app auto-opens and the owner's own team testing. Register all internal testers before the first send.
lessons.evidence: memory.md 245 (Great Spaces looked 'engaged' 6 s after the email, plus a Resend 'click' in the same minute; scanner rules SCANNER_CLICK_SECS=60 and SCANNER_WEB_SECS=30); memory.md 237 (NB 'opened' 20 s after delivery); memory.md 245-247 (Pride card went HOT because of the team's demo test, fixed with an engagement_ignore window); memory.md 225 (Elenza WhatsApp never got any status); only 2 real human page opens in 3 days (Brij 17 Oct 09:02, Pride 19 Oct 09:10).
lessons.do_next_time: Before the first send, put all team phones, IPs and test windows into engagement_ignore.json and tell the owner which signals are noise. Report to him only: page visit after 60 s, video play, button tap, reply, STOP. Keep the rule that an email open never raises a lead's level.

lessons.lesson: How the owner steers: short Hinglish commands, fast decisions, strong standing rules, and he overrides risk-averse advice in favour of speed, presence and both channels. The agent should state the risk once and then comply inside the gate. Positioning errors are cheapest to catch at draft stage, not in the approval message.
lessons.evidence: 123 owner messages 15-19 Oct, median 66 characters, 41 of them 40 characters or fewer; standing orders: 'bas tu meri bato ka jawab deta jaa aur kuch mat puch' (15 Oct 16:17), log every discussion in memory (15 Oct 16:17, 16 Oct 12:52), non-tech UI, live data in the console (17 Oct 09:06, 19 Oct 09:17), owner-quiet because WhatsApp credits (52 owner pings on 15-16 Oct, counters.json). The video-first subject went out on 5 first-touch emails before he caught it at 19 Oct 09:34, two minutes after the 5th.
lessons.do_next_time: Keep a decision register at the top of the campaign file. Before any draft is proposed show 3 lines: what we sell, what the subject promises, the one ask. Answer in at most 10 short Hinglish lines, ask questions only when blocked, and end each work chunk with one line 'what I need from you'.

lessons.lesson: Permission-classifier friction vanished once the work went through ONE door script, one owner-added allow rule and owner-held secrets. The refusals that remain are the correct ones, and each was resolved in minutes by the owner doing the one human-only step.
lessons.evidence: Main-chat classifier denials: 7 on 15-16 Oct (Production Deploy, Create Unsafe Agents x2, 'judged dangerous' x2, Auto-Mode Bypass, Security Weaken), 1 on 19 Oct (Secret-Store Writes), 0 on 17 Oct and 0 during wave 2 (deploy, 8 proposals, 4 sends, 12:03-14:40). The owner pasted failing PowerShell output 6 times on 15-16 Oct and 0 times after. Unattended heartbeat was denied a live send (Real-World Transactions) on 16 Oct 09:41Z. Shell quoting errors are cheap (about 6 heredoc EOFs and 8 Unicode errors in 12 days, seconds each; the one broken QA script string on 19 Oct cost 14 s).
lessons.do_next_time: Keep 'Bash(bash agent/deploy/vps_run.sh *)' in place for the whole campaign. Never try to mint approvals, write secrets, edit settings.local.json or start daemons yourself. Write scripts with the Write tool and set PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8.

lessons.lesson: Free-source research costs more per run, and web-search scouts are the worst. The cheapest source is re-verifying an existing pool. Apify credit of a few dollars buys back about half of the time and tokens. The owner also waited 63 minutes watching the run.

headline: With 9 leads contacted and 0 replies, nothing can be concluded about subject lines, channel order, send time, language or lead type (0/9 only rules out a true reply rate above about 28-34%), and no A/B test can reach significance at 10-12 leads per research round. What the data does show: cold WhatsApp templates are not delivered (0/3), email delivers (11/12) but most engagement signals are machines or our own team, 'zero replies' is not even measured for email, and the one lever never tried at scale is a human voice. The approach is unproven rather than disproven, and it is over-built per lead (about 0.9M sub-agent tokens and a pile of approval codes per contacted lead, zero conversations): next, run about 10 human conversations and a light-vs-heavy comparison with pre-registered decision rules before building more assets or opening campaigns 2-4.

lessons.lesson: With 9 contacted leads, 0 replies and one WhatsApp round still pending, almost nothing is statistically concludable: 0/9 only rules out a true reply rate above about 28-34%, and an A/B between plausible variants needs 30-140 leads per arm while a research round yields 10-12.
lessons.evidence: sends.jsonl = 15 lead sends to 9 leads (5 wave 1, 4 wave 2), max 8 lead sends in a day vs a 10-20/day cap (so lead supply, not the cap, limits n). Exact binomial: 0/9 -> 95% upper bound 34% two-sided (28% one-sided); P(0/9 | true 5%) = 63%, | true 10% = 39%, | true 25% = 8%; 0/21 -> 13%; 0/30 -> 9.5%; 2/9 human page opens -> CI 3-60%; 11/12 emails delivered -> CI 62-100%. Sample size per arm (80% power, alpha 5%): 5% vs 15% = 140, 5% vs 30% = 36, 10% vs 40% = 32, 20% vs 50% = 39. Supply: _research_raw.json 10 leads (14 agents, 34 min, ~2.2M tokens, ~$2.85 Apify), _research_raw_r2.json 12 leads (26 agents, 63 min, ~4.1M tokens, $0) = 22 researched in total.
lessons.do_next_time: (1) Show every rate as k/n with a 95% interval and a 'too early' flag until n_min is reached; never write '0 replies = failed' or '2 opens = promising'. (2) Judge designs on high-base-rate upstream metrics (delivered, qualified human page open, video >50%, CTA tap) where n=30 gives about +/-15-18 points; judge replies by reading each one. (3) Write hypothesis, metric, n_min and the decision rule into the console BEFORE the wave is sent. (4) Keep templates identical across campaigns 2-4 so samples pool (3 x ~12 leads = ~36 per arm) before deciding subject, time or offer. (5) Call the approach failed only after >=21 fully worked leads with 0 positive responses (bound 13%) or >=30 (9.5%); call it working only on named positive conversations (demo asked for, call booked), not on opens.

lessons.lesson: Test hypotheses in order of information per lead (human voice vs email-only, WhatsApp route, light vs heavy assets first) and only LOG subject, send time, offer wording, language and lead type until pooled n is large enough.

lessons.do_next_time: Pre-register these, in this order. H1 CHANNEL: human call or personal WhatsApp by a named team member vs email-only | metric: two-way conversation within 7 days | n_min: 20 calls to describe (+/-22 pts), 32-42 per arm to compare a 10% vs 40% effect. H2 WHATSAPP ROUTE: cold template vs lead-initiated wa.me tap from the email vs human 1:1 | metric: delivered, then CTA/demo start | cold templates are on stop-loss (0/3 + the 15:30 round of 4); count lead-initiated starts per 30 emails. H3 ASSET WEIGHT: heavy (per-lead page + video + designed email) vs light (4-line personal note + one generic page, no per-lead video) | metric: conversations per 10 leads and tokens per lead | descriptive, 9 vs 12. H4 SUBJECT: outcome-first vs video-first | metric: human page open within 72 h | 20% vs 50% needs ~39 per arm, so no test before ~80 sends pooled. H5 SEND TIME: land 08:30-09:30 vs 10:30-11:30 vs afternoon/Fri/Sat | metric: hours to first human open | >=30 per slot (~90 sends); until then just log first_touch_dow/hour. H6 OFFER: free demo (current) vs free 7-day pilot on their own number vs one-question opener | metric: positive reply | >=40 per arm, so only testable with ads or pooled campaigns; owner must define pilot and price first. H7 LANGUAGE: Gujarati voice/text vs English for Gujarati-first leads | ~8 candidates only: descriptive. H8 LEAD TYPE / ROUTE: developer vs reseller/broker/solo owner, and named person or personal mobile vs role inbox | metric: conversation rate | >=20 per class.

lessons.lesson: The approach is unproven, not disproven; its weakest assumption is that a cold, asset-heavy first touch to generic inboxes starts conversations, and the lever never tried at scale is a human voice (call or personal WhatsApp from a named person).
lessons.evidence: Funnel for 9 leads after ~3-4 days: 8 reached by >=1 channel (Elenza dead), 2 unattributed human page opens (Brij 17 Oct 09:02 IST; Pride 19 Oct 09:10 IST + video play), 0 real CTA taps, 0 real demo starts, 0 WhatsApp/CRM replies, 0 stops, 0 complaints.
