Old rule-based CRM baseline: 100 outreached -> 4 engaged + 1 hot (memory G), 87+ emails, 53 WhatsApps to 5 distinct leads.
lessons.do_next_time: Ask the owner to allow a 10-lead human sprint on the Hungry leads (the agent prepares dossier, 4-line script, objection answers, and logs the call; a named team member talks, 5-10 minutes each; send the existing page/video as the leave-behind AFTER the call). Log per call: answered?, decision-maker reached?, how enquiries are handled today (telecallers/CRM/agency), reaction to the offer, objection. Decision schedule (my proposal): 19 Oct 15:30 apply the WhatsApp rule; by 22 Oct (day 3 of wave 2) calls attempted; checkpoint 26 Oct: >=2 positive of >=10 real conversations = continue and scale the segment; 0 positive of >=10 conversations = change offer or segment (campaign 2), not channel; <10 conversations because nobody answers = reachability problem, shift to warm sources; stop touches 5 Nov (Diwali ~8 Nov, playbook). Parallel cheap levers, ranked: (1) call the 5 warm people already in the old CRM (4 engaged + 1 hot) and the 3 clients whose real testimonials sit on the pilot page; (2) a small click-to-WhatsApp ad test pointing at the existing page + demo responder, the only way to get volume for A/B tests of offer wording (hypothesis, needs owner budget, nothing in the files proves it works); (3) agencies that run Meta ads/CRM for developers as a reseller channel (hypothesis; Beverlynn and one dental lead already show agencies in the way). GIHED/CREDAI show was Jan 2026 (R2 scout), outside the window.

lessons.lesson: Engagement numbers are contaminated by link scanners, mail-app auto-opens and our own team, so levels like 'engaged' or 'hot' must come from a qualified-signal rule defined before anyone reads a rate.
lessons.evidence: Great Spaces card 'engaged, opened page 2 times' 6 s after the email left (08:37:34Z -> 08:37:40Z) and a Resend 'click' in the same minute (memory 19 Oct 14:07-14:09); NB and Rivanta emails 'opened' seconds after delivery (email_status.json last_event opened); Pride card HOT (CTA click + demo answers) was the owner's team test, now in engagement_ignore.json; Brij owner click 16 Oct counted as lead use; Pride 'Delivered' came from the boss test (attribution bug fixed 16 Oct). engagement_sync.level_of() still sets 'hot' on any CTA click. After filtering, the real human signal is 2 page opens in 9 leads, neither attributable to a person (no IP or identity stored).
lessons.do_next_time: Define 'qualified signal' = a written reply, an answered call, a CTA/demo from a non-team number, or a page/video event >=60 s after delivery outside ignore windows. Team and owner tests only through a separate test slug or a ?t=1 link that is never counted. Store signal_confidence (certain | probable | uncertain) on every activity row; email open alone = grey, never a level; never mark a lead 'hot' from a web event alone. Keep SCANNER_CLICK_SECS/SCANNER_WEB_SECS and add a rule that two events from different 'devices' inside 10 s of delivery are scanners.

lessons.lesson: 'Zero replies' is not yet a measured zero: email replies go to the Reply-To mailbox (info@ivinfotech.com) that the agent cannot read, and only WhatsApp (CRM) and Resend events are instrumented.
lessons.evidence: memory.md 19 Oct ~13:15: 'replies to the email land in info@ivinfotech.com, which the agent cannot read: someone must watch that mailbox'; all lead emails carry Reply-To info@ (owner_messages/25CU3.txt, 3ZFSQ.txt); engagement_sync.py reads the CRM inbound feed, Resend events and the web log only. 12 of the 15 lead sends were emails.
lessons.do_next_time: Before the next send instrument the reply path: an IMAP read-only poll or an inbound-email webhook on a dedicated reply address, feeding `lead_reply` activity rows with a reply_class (interested | not now | not relevant | stop | wrong person | out-of-office); STOP in an email reply goes to suppress.py automatically. Until built the owner checks the mailbox daily and tells the agent, and the scoreboard shows 'reply path monitored: yes/no' beside every reply count.

lessons.lesson: The hunger score and A/B/C grades are unvalidated sorting heuristics, not predictors: scores compress to 7-8, the skeptic keeps downgrading A leads, and the planned Hungry-vs-Warm comparison was dropped.
lessons.evidence: 14 of 22 scored leads sit at 7-8 (range 4-8; R1 and R2 raw files); skeptic lowered Brij A->B in R1 and six A->B in R2; the campaign entry validation_plan promised wave 2 = Warm leads after a 5-day wait, but wave 2 (19 Oct) is new Hungry leads on day 3; no Warm lead (Beverlynn 6, Silver 6, Lotus 5, Trinetra 5) has been contacted, and 5 vs 4 would have been underpowered anyway. All 9 contacted leads score 7-8, so the score has no variation to test. Every research file repeats 'need is inferred, not observed'.
lessons.do_next_time: Use the score only to sort. To test it, contact a stratified sample (e.g. 15 at >=7 and 15 at <=6) with the same touch and judge only at n>=30; freeze the score at scoring time. When a plan changes (owner reversal, new wave) update campaign.validation_plan in the same step so the stored plan always matches what was run. Do not show 'Hungry 8/10' to the owner as if it were evidence of replies.

lessons.lesson: Reachability (who and what the contact route is) probably matters more than the grade: most routes are role inboxes, webmail or unlabeled phones, and even a 'business-published' address bounced.
lessons.evidence: 12 lead emails -> 11 delivered, 1 bounced (Elenza, address from its own contact page); RERA fresh promoters 150 of 159 use Gmail (_research_raw.json gujrera scout); only ~20 of ~150 Gujarat real-estate advertisers have their own website/email (R2 meta-adlib-browser scout); 10 of 19 rows with an email in trigger_leads_2026-10-14.csv are webmail-only; swarnagroup.in has no MX (R2); Space Age was sent to a personal mobile on purpose because 'the human sees it' (owner 19 Oct 07:27Z); a 5-lead cohort of generic inboxes produced no conversation.
lessons.do_next_time: Record route_type per lead (named_person | personal_mobile | role_inbox | webmail | form_only) and rank leads by route type before grade; run MX plus a mailbox check before the first send; prefer a named decision-maker with a personal mobile for the first human contact. Test 'conversation rate by route type' after >=20 leads per class.

lessons.lesson: Assets-first is an expensive way to learn: each contacted lead consumed about 0.9M sub-agent tokens plus ~25 minutes of build/QA wall-clock and several approval codes, and no conversation resulted; the heavy first touch should be tested against a light one, not assumed.

lessons.lesson: The engine transfers to other verticals and products; the content, the registers and the claim rules are real-estate-specific and must be rebuilt per vertical.
lessons.evidence: TRANSFERS: Meta Ad Library cta_type=WHATSAPP_MESSAGE found 30 leads across 10 verticals in one ~$0.94 run (trigger_leads_2026-10-14.csv, all source=meta_ads); skeptic pass; independent fact-check of the lead's own labels (_wave2_factcheck.json); email stack (MX check, Resend webhook, scanner filter, owner OK codes, owner-quiet mode); slot-filled page/video/demo (leads.json, master_video.html, demo_projects.json); QA lens workflows; small-business contact scarcity (10/19 webmail-only); cold-template failure (Meta policy); explicit 'asks' are rare (R1 and R4: 0-3 per two weeks); India Ad Library shows no spend (R1 meta scout), so pay ability is proxied by ad count/age/page size (dental B grades: 1 ad, 28-155 followers). REAL-ESTATE-SPECIFIC: GujRERA free API (application vs approved date, projectRegId vs projectId, 7/159 business emails), RERA claim rules (say 'scheduled', never 'registered' or 'booked'), unit labels (4B3HK, 2 BHK only, plots in sq yd), developer vs reseller handling (about 87 resellers advertise one project), name collisions (Aaroham), Book Now/site-visit CTA language, launch-timed urgency, Diwali offer season, the narrated video (real-estate wording, needs a new ElevenLabs take per vertical) and the demo question set (budget, type, time, sample buyer card); the Takshashila +40% proof is education, not real estate (proof_points.md).
lessons.do_next_time: For a new vertical keep: research workflow (change CAMPAIGN text and sources), skeptic, fact-check, email/engagement stack, page template, demo responder engine. Rebuild per vertical: hook language and unit labels, demo questions and TEXTS, video narration (one voice take), the proof point, a vertical claim list (medical advertising, subsidy and finance claims), and the hunger rubric weights (re-justify 'funnel gap' for that vertical). Re-verify before reuse: who decides, data-protection sensitivity (clinics hold health data: keep the demo to appointment booking, no patient data in samples). For a different PRODUCT (custom ERP/CRM, websites, apps) the 'paid-enquiry spend' signal does not apply; earlier rounds show explicit asks are rare, so trigger sources (tenders, hiring, registrations) need a fresh test (unsure).

Each campaign: research for >=30 candidates with route_type recorded, 5-call discovery sprint, light note + shared segment page, per-lead assets only after a signal, same template and logging schema so results pool. mistakes_we_made: Built a large tooling stack before a single lead had replied: WhatsApp fast lane + operator lane, a Telegram lane and VPS sandbox kit that could not be connected (owner cannot log in on the web), Agent Console v1/v2 with calendar and bento UI, journey tracker, Resend webhook. The fast lane was abandoned on 16 Oct for credit cost (OWNER_QUIET); with 9 leads a spreadsheet would have shown the same (memory 15-19 Oct).

Sent wave-1 copy before claims were verified: v1 emails used 'your ads' (we do not know who runs the ads; the playbook later banned it), sold 'a short video' in the subject (owner caught it 19 Oct 04:04Z), and Brij's v1 states the ads open a WhatsApp chat. The independent fact-check only started in wave 2, after 5 leads had been contacted; the video narration still says 'gets', 'free', 'your WhatsApp ads' (accepted known issue for Great Spaces and Parshwanath).

No stop-loss after the first template failure: Brij was marked 131049 at ~15:20 on 16 Oct yet NB (15:39) and Elenza (16:35) were still sent, and wave 2 schedules four more, although the 14 Oct blueprint predicted the failure and the playbook defaulted to email first.

Put the boss's personal number on four live landing pages (WhatsApp button and call line) and listed it as a test target; caught after deployment and fixed the same day (FORBIDDEN_NUMBERS build guard added).

Reported false signals to the owner as facts: Pride 'Delivered' (boss-test attribution bug), Brij page use (the owner's own click), Great Spaces 'engaged' 6 s after send (link scanner), Pride 'HOT' (team test), email 'opened' (auto-open), and a heartbeat told the owner 'lead got nothing' when the send had gone out (race, 16 Oct).

Presented hunger scores (for example 'Hungry 8/10') with false precision: the same agent that found the lead scored it, 14 of 22 sit at 7-8, the skeptic lowered A grades 7 times, and the Hungry-vs-Warm validation plan was silently dropped without updating the campaign entry.

Chose send times by availability, not evidence: Friday 16:29-16:35 and Saturday 10:05 for wave 1, Monday 14:07 for wave 2; the QA-advised 3 h gap before WhatsApp was cut to ~80 min on owner instruction without recording it as an experiment.
Skipped MX/mailbox verification in round 1: Elenza's published address bounced; the MX check only arrived in round 2 (which found Swarna has none).
Burned an approval code (WX85U) because the app id was read after the code was consumed, let one expire unsent (HNDWP), and issued 28 codes for 15 lead sends.
Never instrumented the email reply path (Reply-To info@): the 'zero replies' statement is unverified for the channel that carried 12 of 15 lead sends.

Wrote an optimistic campaign plan (daily cap 10, template-only first touch, Hungry then Warm after 5 days) that was overtaken by owner reversals within four days and never updated, so the stored plan cannot be evaluated.
